Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 30, verses 6–7:

As for knowledge of God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the details of these, it is conveyed through the messengers. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿God's promise. God does not break His promise, but most people do not know. They know an outward aspect of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter.﴾

One of the early generations (al-salaf) said: "One of them has so much knowledge of the world that he can tap a dirham with his fingernail and know its weight, yet he has no knowledge of any part of his religion."

God, exalted is He, also said about the knowledge of these people and their delusion through it: ﴿So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had, and there encompassed them that which they used to mock.﴾ [Ghafir: 83] God has varied greatly among His servants in what their minds and intellects can attain. The intellect gives its owner benefit in the type of knowledge he is bound to, occupied with, and confined to, what it does not give him in other fields, even if those other fields are much easier than his. It gives him what his resolve and natural aptitude give him in the craft he is concerned with and focused on, and not what it gives him in another craft.

You often find a man who excels in the subtle branches of knowledge and inquiry, yet falls short in the grand ones. He hits the most obscure and finest points while missing the most important and evident ones.

This is a matter that is plain to see. How much more so, then, are the knowledge and insights of the prophets beyond the reach of the intellect? Although the intellect cannot independently grasp them, it does not reject them. Rather, when they are presented to it, it acknowledges their truth, hastens to accept them, and submits to them. It also knows that the knowledge attained by people through their own reasoning, compared to theirs, is like the knowledge of children compared to that of these prophets, a difference beyond measure.

(Question)

If you ask: how can firm, undoubting belief in the Return, Paradise, and Hell coexist with the neglect of action?

Is it in human nature that a servant knows he will be brought tomorrow before some king who will either punish him with the most severe punishment or honor him with the fullest honor, and yet he spends the night heedless and unaware, not remembering his standing before the king, not preparing for it, and not taking his provisions for it?

It is said: by God's life, this is a valid question, which applies to most of this creation. The combination of these two matters is among the most astonishing things. This failure has several causes:

The first: weakness of knowledge and lack of certainty. Whoever thinks that knowledge does not vary in strength has a statement that is among the most corrupt and invalid.

Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil) asked his Lord to show him the raising of the dead with his own eyes, even though he already knew the Lord's power to do so, so that his tranquility would increase and what was known by reasoning would become something witnessed.

Ahmad related in his Musnad from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The report is not like seeing with one's own eyes."

When weakness of knowledge is combined with failure to keep it present, or with its absence from the heart for much or most of the time because one is occupied with what opposes it, and when this is joined by the pull of natural desire, the overpowering of passions, the dominance of lust, the whispering of the self, the deception of Satan, the slowness of the promise to come, the length of hope, the slumber of heedlessness, the love of what is immediate, the leniency of interpretations, and the familiarity of habits, then at that point nothing holds faith except the One who holds the heavens and the earth from falling. For this reason people differ in faith and deeds, to the point of being reduced to the smallest weight of a mustard seed in the heart.

All these causes ultimately return to weakness of insight and patience. For this reason God, glorified is He, praised the people of patience and certainty and made them leaders in religion. He said: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs.﴾ [Sajda: 24]

(Exhortation)

It is astonishing, and utterly astonishing, that someone should be heedless when his moments are counted against him, and every breath he takes is valueless once it is gone and does not return to him. The mounts of night and day hurry him along, yet he does not reflect where he is being carried and driven. Their pace is faster than the post-rider's. He does not know to which of the two abodes he will be transferred. When death comes upon him, his anxiety intensifies over the ruin of his body and the loss of his pleasures, not over the offenses he committed before or the neglect he showed in not providing for his life. When a passing thought of what he was created for crosses his mind, he dismisses it by relying on forgiveness, saying: "We have been told that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful," as though he was never told that His punishment is the painful torment.

When a passing thought of what he was created for crosses his mind, he dismisses it by relying on forgiveness, saying: "We have been told that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful," as though he was never told that His punishment is the painful torment.

(Chapter: On convening a session containing a debate between the advocate of singing and the advocate of the Qur'an)

The advocate of listening (al-sama') said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day they will be divided (14). As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, rejoicing (15).﴾

It is related in the tafsir that this [meadow of rejoicing] is listening (al-sama'), and if it were forbidden, it would not be among the finest bliss of Paradise.

The advocate of the Qur'an said: If you had refrained from your argument for the soundness of what you have adopted, it would have been more concealing for it and more marketable among those whose share of insight and knowledge is small. But Allah refuses except to expose it and lay it bare upon your tongues.

Without doubt, some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: The "rejoicing" here is listening to beautiful singing in Paradise, and that the houris (al-hur al-'in) will sing with voices such as no creatures have ever heard as more beautiful than them. They will say: "We are the everlasting, so we shall not die; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him."

Abu Nu'aym mentioned in "Sifat al-Jannah," from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Indeed, the wives of the people of Paradise will sing to their husbands with the most beautiful voices anyone has ever heard. Among what they sing is: 'We are the good and beautiful ones; we are the wives of noble people, who look with eyes cool with delight.' And among what they sing is: 'We are the everlasting, so they shall never die; we are the secure, so they shall never fear; we are the abiding, so they shall never depart.'"
Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam alone narrated it.

He also narrated, through the route of al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr: Sa'd al-Ta'i related to me from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit from Ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned a hadith in which: "The houris will gather every seven days, and they will say with beautiful voices no creatures have ever heard the like of: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; we are the abiding, so we shall not depart; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"

He also narrated, through the route of Ibn Abi Fudayk from Ibn Abi Dhi'b from 'Awn ibn al-Khattab from a son of Anas, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The houris will sing in Paradise: 'We are the beautiful ones, created for noble husbands.'"

And through the route of Zayd ibn Waqid from a man, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree whose trunks are of gold and whose branches are of chrysolite and pearls. A wind blows upon it and it sways, and no listeners have ever heard a sound sweeter than it."

And through the route of Khalid ibn Ma'dan from Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said:
"No servant enters Paradise but that two houris sit at his head and at his feet, singing to him with the most beautiful voice heard by mankind and jinn, and it is not like the flutes of Satan."

al-Tirmidhi related: Ahmad ibn Mani' related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq related to us from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a gathering place for the houris, who raise voices the creatures have never heard the like of," and he said: "They say: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"
He said: It is a gharib hadith.

al-Tabarani related from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Abi Karimah (in whom there is some discussion), from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah! Are the women of this world better, or the houris?" He said: "Rather, the women of this world are better than the houris, as the superiority of the outer garment over the inner lining." I said: "O Messenger of Allah! And why is that?" He said: "Because of their prayers, their fasting, and their worship of Allah. Allah clothes their faces in light and their bodies in silk, white of colour, green garments, yellow ornaments, their censers are of pearl, and their combs are of gold. They say: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not die; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall never be miserable; we are the abiding, so we shall never depart; we are the ones content, so we shall never be angry; blessed is he for whom we were and who was for us.'" The hadith continues.

It is said to you: Does it follow that what Allah bestows upon His servants in the Hereafter is permissible for them in this world?

If you say: It does not follow, then your argument collapses.

And if you say: It follows, it is said to you: Allah, glory be to Him, bestows upon them in the Hereafter garments of silk and bracelets of gold. So permit them to wear these in this world, and oppose His religion and His command. Also, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestows upon them wine in Paradise; so permit them to drink it in this world, by the same reasoning. Also, they eat and drink in Paradise from vessels of gold and silver, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "These are theirs in this world, and ours in the Hereafter." Extending your position, that since these are for the Muslims in the Hereafter they are permissible in this world, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever drinks wine in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter," and "Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter," and he said concerning vessels of gold and silver: "These are for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter."

Thus he informed that whoever uses these things in this world, whether food, clothing or other, will not use them in the Hereafter. Either the people of Paradise use them and he is deprived of them even if he enters it, as Ibn Abi Hatim related: my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami related to us, al-Hasan, i.e. Ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Bazzaz, related to us from Humayd al-Kharrat from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "Whoever drinks it in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter."

He (the objector) said: "But he repented, until Allah admitted him to Paradise, and Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And therein you shall have whatever your souls desire, and therein you shall have whatever you ask for﴾ [Fussilat: 31]."

He (the respondent) said: Allah will make them forget it.

Or else that is a threat to him that he will not enter Paradise, for these things are used by the people of Paradise, so whoever does not obtain them in the Hereafter is not among the people of Paradise. These are two interpretations of the early generations concerning these hadiths.

So if it were said: this delightful listening promised in Paradise belongs only to whoever purified his hearing in this world from listening to singing and entertainments, by analogy with its counterpart in clothing, drinking wine and using vessels of gold and silver, this would be closer to the truth and more sound than your argument for its permissibility in this world based on the people of Paradise using it.

The report has indeed come explicitly in support of what we have said, namely what Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya related: Dawud ibn 'Amr al-Dabbi related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us from Malik ibn Anas from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Where are those who used to purify themselves from frivolity and the flutes of Satan? Settle them in gardens of musk.' Then He will say to the angels: 'Let them hear My praise and My glorification, and inform them that there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.'" And its transmission from Mujahid has already been mentioned, from the words of Ibn Battah.

Also, it has come in a hadith that a man among the people of Paradise will be married to seventy-two wives. Abu Nu'aym mentioned it in the book Sifat al-Jannah, from the hadith of Khalid ibn Ma'dan from Abu Umamah from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "No servant enters Paradise but that he is married to seventy-two wives: two of them from the houris and seventy from the people of his inheritance from the people of this world, none of whom is a woman but that she has a delightful sexual pleasure, and he has a member that does not grow limp."

And it was mentioned from the hadith of al-Hajjaj, from Qatadah, from Anas, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The believer in Paradise will have thirty wives." We said: "O Messenger of Allah! Will he have the strength for that?" He said: "Indeed he will be given the strength of a hundred."

In another hadith: "Indeed a man among them will reach a hundred virgins in a single day."

These reports do not contradict one another, for their differences in number correspond to their differences in the measure of reward. Therefore, by the analogy of those who argue for the permissibility of listening to singing in this world on the ground that it belongs to the people of Paradise, they should likewise permit a man in this world to marry this number. End of quotation.

(Chapter: On mentioning the listening of Paradise and the singing of the houris, and what it contains of ecstasy and delight)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day they will be divided. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, rejoicing.﴾

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi related to me, 'Amir ibn Nassaf related to us, who said: I asked Yahya ibn Abi Kathir about the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿they will be in a meadow, rejoicing﴾. He said: "al-hibrah is delight, and listening." 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi related to us, Dhamrah ibn Rabi'ah related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding His words "yuhbarun" (they will be made to rejoice), who said: "Listening in Paradise." This does not contradict the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, "yukramun" (they will be honoured), nor the saying of Mujahid and Qatadah, "yun'amun" (they will be made to enjoy bliss); the delight of the ear through listening is part of the "hibrah" and the bliss.

al-Tirmidhi related: Hannad and Ahmad ibn Mani' related to us, both said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq related to us from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Indeed, in Paradise there is a gathering place for the houris, who raise their voices with sounds the creatures have never heard the like of, saying: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"

Concerning this topic (al-bab), there are reports from Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, and Anas, and the hadith of 'Ali is gharib.

I say: On this topic there are also reports from Ibn Abi Awfa, Abu Umamah, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Ja'far al-Firyabi said: Sa'd ibn Hafs related to us, Muhammad ibn Maslamah related to us from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "In Paradise there is a river the length of Paradise, whose banks are maidens standing facing one another, singing with voices until the creatures hear them, and they see no delight in Paradise like it." We said: "O Abu Hurayrah, and what is that singing?" He said: "Glorification, praise, sanctification, and thanksgiving to the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, if Allah wills."
Thus he narrated it as a mawquf report.

Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah related from the hadith of Maslamah ibn 'Ali, from Zayd ibn Waqid, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree whose trunks are of gold and whose branches are of chrysolite and pearls; a wind blows upon it and they sway, and no listeners have ever heard a sound sweeter than it."

As for the hadith of Anas, Abu Nu'aym said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim related to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us from Ibn Abi Dhi'b from 'Awn ibn al-Khattab from 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' from Abu al-Asan from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"The houris will sing in Paradise, saying: 'We are the beautiful houris, created for noble husbands.'"
Ibn Abi al-Dunya also related it: Abu Khaythamah related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Umar related to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b related to us from Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' from some of the children of Anas, and he mentioned it.

As for the hadith of Ibn Abi Awfa, Abu Nu'aym said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us from its origin, Musa ibn Harun related to us, Hamid ibn Yahya al-Balkhi related to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib related to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr related to us, and Sa'd al-Ta'i related to me from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit from Ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Every one of the people of Paradise will be married to four thousand virgins, eight thousand widows, and a hundred houris, and they will gather every seven days and say with beautiful voices no creatures have ever heard the like of: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; we are the abiding, so we shall not depart; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"

As for the hadith of Abu Umamah, Ja'far al-Firyabi said: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, Khalid ibn Yazid related to us from Abu Malik from his father from Khalid ibn Ma'dan from Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said:
"No servant enters Paradise but that two houris sit at his head and at his feet, singing to him with the most beautiful voice heard by mankind and jinn, and it is not like the flutes of Satan."

As for the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, al-Tabarani said: Abu Rifa'ah 'Ammarah ibn Wathimah ibn Musa ibn al-Furat al-Misri related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Indeed the wives of the people of Paradise will sing to their husbands with the most beautiful voices anyone has ever heard. Among what they sing is: 'We are the good and beautiful ones, wives of noble people, who look with eyes cool with delight.' And among what they sing is: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall never die; we are the secure, so we shall never fear; we are the abiding, so we shall never depart.'"
al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from Zayd ibn Aslam except Muhammad; Ibn Abi Maryam alone narrated it.

Ibn Wahb said: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub related to me, and a man from Quraysh said to Ibn Shihab: "Is there listening in Paradise? For listening has been made beloved to me." He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn Shihab, in Paradise there are trees whose fruit is pearls and chrysolite, and beneath them are buxom maidens singing in varied tones, saying: 'We are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the everlasting, so we shall not die,' singing in varied tones. When that tree hears this, its branches clap against one another, and the maidens are rendered silent, so we do not know whether the voices of the maidens are more beautiful or the voices of the tree."

Ibn Wahb said: al-Layth ibn Sa'd related to us from Khalid ibn Yazid: "The houris will sing to their husbands, saying: 'We are the good and beautiful ones, the wives of young noble men; we are the everlasting, so we shall not die; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; we are the abiding, so we shall not depart,' and on the breast of each of them is written: 'You are my beloved, and I am your beloved; my soul has ended at you; my eyes have never seen the likes of you.'"

Ibn al-Mubarak said: al-Awza'i related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us: "The houris will meet their husbands at the gates of Paradise, saying: 'How long we have awaited you! We are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; the abiding, so we shall not depart; the everlasting, so we shall not die,' with the most beautiful voices, and he says: 'You are my beloved, and I am your beloved; there is none beside you who falls short, and none beyond you who is equal.'"

(Chapter: They have a listening higher than this)

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Dahtham ibn al-Fadl al-Qurashi related to me, al-Awza'i related to us, who said: "It has reached me that there is no creature of God with a more beautiful voice than Israfil. God, Blessed and Exalted, commands him, and he begins to sing, and no angel in the heavens remains without interrupting his prayer to listen. He remains thus for as long as God wills, and then God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'By My might and My majesty, if the servants knew the measure of My greatness, they would not worship other than Me.'" And Dawud ibn 'Amr al-Dabbi related to me: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us from Malik ibn Anas from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Where are those who used to purify their hearing and their souls from the assemblies of Allah and the flutes of Satan? Settle them in gardens of musk.' Then He will say to the angels: 'Let them hear My glorification and My praise.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan related to me, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to me, Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Malik ibn Dinar regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾ [Sad: 40]. He said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a high pulpit will be placed in Paradise, and it will be announced: 'O Dawud, glorify Me with that beautiful, resonant voice with which you used to glorify Me in the abode of the world.' So the voice of Dawud will exhaust the bliss of the people of the gardens." This is His words, the Exalted: ﴿So We forgave him that, and indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾.

Hammad ibn Salamah mentioned, from Thabit al-Bunani and Hajjaj al-Aswad, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Indeed Allah, may His praise be great, says to the angels: "Indeed My servants used to love beautiful voices in the world, and they would call upon it for My sake. So let My servants hear, and they will take up sounds of tahlil, tasbih and takbir such as they have never heard the like of."

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in Kitab al-Zuhd of his father: 'Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi related to me, Sayyar related to me, Ja'far related to us, Malik ibn Dinar related to us, regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾. He said: "Allah, glory be to Him, will station Dawud at the foot of the Throne, and say: 'O Dawud, glorify Me today with that beautiful, resonant voice.' He will say: 'My God, how can I glorify You when You took it from me in the abode of the world?' He will say: 'Indeed I will return it to you.' He will return it to him, and his voice will increase. So the voice of Dawud will exhaust the bliss of the people of Paradise."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim al-Harrani related to us, Miskin ibn Bukayr related to us from al-Awza'i from 'Ubaydah ibn Abi Lubabah, who said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a tree whose fruit is chrysolite, ruby and pearls. Allah sends a wind, and it sways, and there is heard from it sounds such as none has heard sweeter."

Abu Bakr ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Sa'id related to us, both said: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi related to us, Rif'ah ibn Salih related to us from Salamah ibn Zuhram from 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 30, verse 14–16 (part 2 of 2):

"In Paradise there is a tree on a trunk, so large that a rider could travel in its shade for a hundred years. They will converse in its shade, and one of them will desire something and mention the frivolities of the world, and God will send a wind from Paradise that moves that tree with every frivolity that existed in the world."

Ibn Abi Shaybah... [Note: the isnad as given reads] Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Sa'id al-Harithi narrated to me, he said:

"It has been related to me that in Paradise there are thickets of reed made of gold, whose sheaths are pearls. When the people of Paradise desire to hear a beautiful sound, God will send over those thickets a wind that brings them every sound they desire."

(Section)

For them there is a hearing higher than this, before which every other hearing fades away. This is when they hear the speech of their Lord, majestic is His majesty, His address, His peace upon them, His speaking with them, and His recitation of His speech to them. When they hear it from Him, it is as though they had never heard it before. There will pass before you, O Sunni reader, among the sound and fair hadiths on this matter, what is among the most beloved hearing to you in this world, the sweetest to your ears, and the most comforting to your eye, for there is no pleasure in Paradise greater than gazing upon the face of the Lord, exalted is He, and hearing His speech from Him. The people of Paradise will be given nothing more beloved to them than this.

Abu al-Shaykh has mentioned, from Salih ibn Hibban, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, who said:

"The people of Paradise enter upon the Almighty, majestic is His majesty, twice every day, and the Qur'an is recited to them. Each one of them sits in his own seat, which is upon pulpits of pearl, ruby, chrysolite, gold and emerald. Their eyes are not comforted by anything, and they have never heard anything greater or more beautiful than it. Then they return to their dwellings, comfortable, their eyes content, until the same time the following day."

(Chapter: On mentioning the listening of Paradise and the singing of the houris, and what it contains of ecstasy and delight)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day they will be divided. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, rejoicing.﴾

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi related to me, 'Amir ibn Nassaf related to us, who said: I asked Yahya ibn Abi Kathir about the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿they will be in a meadow, rejoicing﴾. He said: "al-hibrah is delight, and listening." 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi related to us, Dhamrah ibn Rabi'ah related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding His words "yuhbarun" (they will be made to rejoice), who said: "Listening in Paradise." al-Tirmidhi related: Hannad and Ahmad ibn Mani' related to us, both said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq related to us from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Indeed, in Paradise there is a gathering place for the houris, who raise their voices with sounds the creatures have never heard the like of, saying: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"

Concerning this topic (al-bab), there are reports from Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, and Anas, and the hadith of 'Ali is gharib.

I say: On this topic there are also reports from Ibn Abi Awfa, Abu Umamah, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Ja'far al-Firyabi said: Sa'd ibn Hafs related to us, Muhammad ibn Maslamah related to us from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "In Paradise there is a river the length of Paradise, whose banks are maidens standing facing one another, singing with voices until the creatures hear them, and they see no delight in Paradise like it." We said: "O Abu Hurayrah, and what is that singing?" He said: "Glorification, praise, sanctification, and thanksgiving to the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, if Allah wills."
Thus he narrated it as a mawquf report.

Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah related from the hadith of Maslamah ibn 'Ali, from Zayd ibn Waqid, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree whose trunks are of gold and whose branches are of chrysolite and pearls; a wind blows upon it and they sway, and no listeners have ever heard a sound sweeter than it."

As for the hadith of Anas, Abu Nu'aym said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim related to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us from Ibn Abi Dhi'b from 'Awn ibn al-Khattab from 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' from Abu al-Asan from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Every one of the people of Paradise will be married to four thousand virgins, eight thousand widows, and a hundred houris, and they will gather every seven days and say with beautiful voices no creatures have ever heard the like of: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; we are the abiding, so we shall not depart; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"

As for the hadith of Abu Umamah, Ja'far al-Firyabi said: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, Khalid ibn Yazid related to us from Abu Malik from his father from Khalid ibn Ma'dan from Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said:
"No servant enters Paradise but that two houris sit at his head and at his feet, singing to him with the most beautiful voice heard by mankind and jinn, and it is not like the flutes of Satan."

As for the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, al-Tabarani said: Abu Rifa'ah 'Ammarah ibn Wathimah ibn Musa ibn al-Furat al-Misri related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Indeed the wives of the people of Paradise will sing to their husbands with the most beautiful voices anyone has ever heard. Among what they sing is: 'We are the good and beautiful ones, wives of noble people, who look with eyes cool with delight.' He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn Shihab, in Paradise there are trees whose fruit is pearls and chrysolite, and beneath them are buxom maidens singing in varied tones, saying: 'We are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the everlasting, so we shall not die,' singing in varied tones. "It has been related to me that in Paradise there are thickets of reed made of gold, whose sheaths are pearls. When the people of Paradise desire to hear a beautiful sound, God will send over those thickets a wind that brings them every sound they desire."

(Section)

For them there is a hearing higher than this, before which every other hearing fades away. This is when they hear the speech of their Lord, majestic is His majesty, His address, His peace upon them, His speaking with them, and His recitation of His speech to them. When they hear it from Him, it is as though they had never heard it before. Abu al-Shaykh has mentioned, from Salih ibn Hibban, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, who said:

"The people of Paradise enter upon the Almighty, majestic is His majesty, twice every day, and the Qur'an is recited to them. Each one of them sits in his own seat, which is upon pulpits of pearl, ruby, chrysolite, gold and emerald. Their eyes are not comforted by anything, and they have never heard anything greater or more beautiful than it. Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah related from the hadith of Maslamah ibn 'Ali, from Zayd ibn Waqid, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree whose trunks are of gold and whose branches are of chrysolite and pearls; a wind blows upon it and they sway, and no listeners have ever heard a sound sweeter than it."

As for the hadith of Anas, Abu Nu'aym said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far informed us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim related to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us from Ibn Abi Dhi'b from 'Awn ibn al-Khattab from 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' from Abu al-Asan from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"The houris will sing in Paradise, saying: 'We are the beautiful houris, created for noble husbands.'"
Ibn Abi al-Dunya also related it: Abu Khaythamah related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Umar related to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b related to us from Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' from some of the children of Anas, and he mentioned it.

As for the hadith of Ibn Abi Awfa, Abu Nu'aym said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us from its origin, Musa ibn Harun related to us, Hamid ibn Yahya al-Balkhi related to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib related to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr related to us, and Sa'd al-Ta'i related to me from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit from Ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Every one of the people of Paradise will be married to four thousand virgins, eight thousand widows, and a hundred houris, and they will gather every seven days and say with beautiful voices no creatures have ever heard the like of: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall not perish; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; we are the abiding, so we shall not depart; blessed is he who was for us and we were for him.'"

As for the hadith of Abu Umamah, Ja'far al-Firyabi said: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, Khalid ibn Yazid related to us from Abu Malik from his father from Khalid ibn Ma'dan from Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said:
"No servant enters Paradise but that two houris sit at his head and at his feet, singing to him with the most beautiful voice heard by mankind and jinn, and it is not like the flutes of Satan."

As for the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, al-Tabarani said: Abu Rifa'ah 'Ammarah ibn Wathimah ibn Musa ibn al-Furat al-Misri related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us from Zayd ibn Aslam from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Indeed the wives of the people of Paradise will sing to their husbands with the most beautiful voices anyone has ever heard. Among what they sing is: 'We are the good and beautiful ones, wives of noble people, who look with eyes cool with delight.' And among what they sing is: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall never die; we are the secure, so we shall never fear; we are the abiding, so we shall never depart.'"
al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from Zayd ibn Aslam except Muhammad; Ibn Abi Maryam alone narrated it.

Ibn Wahb said: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub related to me, and a man from Quraysh said to Ibn Shihab: "Is there listening in Paradise? For listening has been made beloved to me." He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Ibn Shihab, in Paradise there are trees whose fruit is pearls and chrysolite, and beneath them are buxom maidens singing in varied tones, saying: 'We are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the everlasting, so we shall not die,' singing in varied tones. When that tree hears this, its branches clap against one another, and the maidens are rendered silent, so we do not know whether the voices of the maidens are more beautiful or the voices of the tree."

Ibn Wahb said: al-Layth ibn Sa'd related to us from Khalid ibn Yazid: "The houris will sing to their husbands, saying: 'We are the good and beautiful ones, the wives of young noble men; we are the everlasting, so we shall not die; we are the ones in bliss, so we shall not be miserable; we are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; we are the abiding, so we shall not depart,' and on the breast of each of them is written: 'You are my beloved, and I am your beloved; my soul has ended at you; my eyes have never seen the likes of you.'"

Ibn al-Mubarak said: al-Awza'i related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us: "The houris will meet their husbands at the gates of Paradise, saying: 'How long we have awaited you! We are the ones content, so we shall not be angry; the abiding, so we shall not depart; the everlasting, so we shall not die,' with the most beautiful voices, and he says: 'You are my beloved, and I am your beloved; there is none beside you who falls short, and none beyond you who is equal.'"

(Chapter: They have a listening higher than this)

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Dahtham ibn al-Fadl al-Qurashi related to me, al-Awza'i related to us, who said: "It has reached me that there is no creature of God with a more beautiful voice than Israfil. God, Blessed and Exalted, commands him, and he begins to sing, and no angel in the heavens remains without interrupting his prayer to listen. He remains thus for as long as God wills, and then God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'By My might and My majesty, if the servants knew the measure of My greatness, they would not worship other than Me.'" And Dawud ibn 'Amr al-Dabbi related to me: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us from Malik ibn Anas from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Where are those who used to purify their hearing and their souls from the assemblies of Allah and the flutes of Satan? Settle them in gardens of musk.' Then He will say to the angels: 'Let them hear My glorification and My praise.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan related to me, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to me, Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Malik ibn Dinar regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾ [Sad: 40]. He said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a high pulpit will be placed in Paradise, and it will be announced: 'O Dawud, glorify Me with that beautiful, resonant voice with which you used to glorify Me in the abode of the world.' So the voice of Dawud will exhaust the bliss of the people of the gardens." This is His words, the Exalted: ﴿So We forgave him that, and indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾.

Hammad ibn Salamah mentioned, from Thabit al-Bunani and Hajjaj al-Aswad, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Indeed Allah, may His praise be great, says to the angels: "Indeed My servants used to love beautiful voices in the world, and they would call upon it for My sake. So let My servants hear, and they will take up sounds of tahlil, tasbih and takbir such as they have never heard the like of."

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in Kitab al-Zuhd of his father: 'Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi related to me, Sayyar related to me, Ja'far related to us, Malik ibn Dinar related to us, regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return﴾. He said: "Allah, glory be to Him, will station Dawud at the foot of the Throne, and say: 'O Dawud, glorify Me today with that beautiful, resonant voice.' He will say: 'My God, how can I glorify You when You took it from me in the abode of the world?' He will say: 'Indeed I will return it to you.' He will return it to him, and his voice will increase. So the voice of Dawud will exhaust the bliss of the people of Paradise."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim al-Harrani related to us, Miskin ibn Bukayr related to us from al-Awza'i from 'Ubaydah ibn Abi Lubabah, who said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a tree whose fruit is chrysolite, ruby and pearls. Allah sends a wind, and it sways, and there is heard from it sounds such as none has heard sweeter."

Abu Bakr ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Sa'id related to us, both said: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi related to us, Rif'ah ibn Salih related to us from Salamah ibn Zuhram from 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 30, verse 14–16 (part 2 of 2):

"In Paradise there is a tree on a trunk, so large that a rider could travel in its shade for a hundred years. They will converse in its shade, and one of them will desire something and mention the frivolities of the world, and God will send a wind from Paradise that moves that tree with every frivolity that existed in the world."

Ibn Abi Shaybah... [Note: the isnad as given reads] Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Sa'id al-Harithi narrated to me, he said:

"It has been related to me that in Paradise there are thickets of reed made of gold, whose sheaths are pearls. When the people of Paradise desire to hear a beautiful sound, God will send over those thickets a wind that brings them every sound they desire."

(Section)

For them there is a hearing higher than this, before which every other hearing fades away. This is when they hear the speech of their Lord, majestic is His majesty, His address, His peace upon them, His speaking with them, and His recitation of His speech to them. When they hear it from Him, it is as though they had never heard it before. There will pass before you, O Sunni reader, among the sound and fair hadiths on this matter, what is among the most beloved hearing to you in this world, the sweetest to your ears, and the most comforting to your eye, for there is no pleasure in Paradise greater than gazing upon the face of the Lord, exalted is He, and hearing His speech from Him. The people of Paradise will be given nothing more beloved to them than this.

Abu al-Shaykh has mentioned, from Salih ibn Hibban, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, who said:

"The people of Paradise enter upon the Almighty, majestic is His majesty, twice every day, and the Qur'an is recited to them. Each one of them sits in his own seat, which is upon pulpits of pearl, ruby, chrysolite, gold and emerald. Their eyes are not comforted by anything, and they have never heard anything greater or more beautiful than it. Then they return to their dwellings, comfortable, their eyes content, until the same time the following day."

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 30, verse 21 (part 1 of 2):**

[Section: The Love of Wives]

As for love for wives, there is no blame upon the one who loves them in this regard. Rather, it is part of his perfection. Allah, glorified is He, has bestowed favour upon His servants through it, saying:

﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ [al-Rum: 21].

He made the woman a resting place for the man, in whom his heart finds rest, and He placed between them pure love, which is affection joined with mercy. And Allah, exalted is He, said after mentioning what is lawful for us of women and what is forbidden of them:

﴿Allah wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. And Allah wants to turn to you in forgiveness, but those who follow their desires want you to deviate with a great deviation. Allah wants to lighten for you, and man was created weak.﴾ [al-Nisa: 26-28].

Sufyan al-Thawri mentioned in his tafsir (exegesis), from Ibn Tawus, from his father: "When he looked at women, he could not be patient."

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that "he saw a woman, so he went to Zaynab and fulfilled his need with her, and said: 'Indeed the woman approaches in the form of a devil and withdraws in the form of a devil. So when one of you sees a woman and she pleases him, let him go to his wife, for that will turn back what is in his soul.'"

In this hadith there are several benefits:

Among them: guidance to find solace for what is desired through its own kind, just as food takes the place of food and a garment takes the place of a garment.

And among them: the command to treat the admiration of a woman, which inherits desire for her, with the most beneficial remedy, which is fulfilling one's need from one's wife. This breaks his desire for her. This is like the guidance given to lovers toward marriage, as in the Sunan of Ibn Majah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "No example has been seen for lovers like marriage."

So marrying the beloved is the remedy for passionate love, which Allah has made a lawful remedy. Dawud (peace be upon him) also sought this remedy, and the Prophet of Allah did not commit anything forbidden. Rather, he married the woman and joined her to his wives because of his love for her. His repentance was in accordance with his high station with Allah and the loftiness of his rank. It does not befit us to say more than this.

As for the story of Zaynab bint Jahsh: Zayd had resolved to divorce her, and she did not agree to him. He used to consult the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about separating from her, and he (ﷺ) would command him to keep her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knew that he would certainly separate from her, so he concealed in himself that he would marry her once Zayd had separated from her. He feared the people's talk: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had married his son's wife, for he had adopted Zayd before prophethood. The Lord, exalted is He, wished to legislate a general law containing the benefits of His servants. When Zayd divorced her and her waiting period ended, he (ﷺ) sent someone to propose to her on his own behalf. Zayd came and stood with his back to the door, and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had mentioned about her weighed on his chest. He called to her from behind the door: "O Zaynab, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is proposing to you." She said: "I will do nothing until I consult my Lord." She stood at her prayer niche and prayed. So Allah, mighty and majestic, Himself undertook her marriage to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and concluded the marriage for him above His Throne. The revelation came with this:

﴿So when Zayd had no further need of her, We married her to you.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then immediately rose and entered upon her. She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) about this, saying: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens." This is the story of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Zaynab.

There is no doubt that the Prophet (ﷺ) had been made to love women, as in the Sahih, from Anas, from him (ﷺ):

"Of your world, women and perfume have been made beloved to me, and the coolness of my eyes has been placed in prayer."

This is the wording of the hadith, not what some narrate as: "Three things from your world have been made beloved to me."

Imam Ahmad added in Kitab al-Zuhd in this hadith:

"I endure hunger and thirst patiently, but I cannot be patient regarding them."

The enemies of Allah, the Jews, envied him for this and said: "His only concern is marriage." So Allah, glorified is He, repelled this from His Messenger (ﷺ) and defended him, saying:

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? Indeed We gave the family of Ibrahim the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom.﴾ [al-Nisa: 54].

And this is the Friend of Allah, Ibrahim, who had with him Sarah, the most beautiful of the women of the worlds, and he loved Hajar and took her as a concubine.

And this is Dawud (peace be upon him), who had ninety-nine women, then he loved that one woman and married her, thus completing the hundred. And this is his son Sulayman (peace be upon him), who used to go around to ninety women in one night.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the most beloved of people to him, and he said: "Aisha," (may Allah be pleased with her). And he said about Khadija: "Indeed I have been granted her love."

So the love of women is part of human perfection. Ibn Abbas said: "The best of this Ummah is the one with the most wives." Imam Ahmad mentioned that Abdullah ibn Umar, on the day of Jalula', received as his share a slave girl whose neck was like a silver ewer. Abdullah said: "I could not restrain myself from kissing her while people were watching." By this, Imam Ahmad argued for the permissibility of enjoying a captive woman before her istibra' (the waiting period to establish she is not pregnant), by means other than intercourse, unlike a purchased slave girl.

The difference between them is that the cancellation of ownership is not supposed in the case of a captive, unlike a purchased one, since ownership may be cancelled in her case, so one would be enjoying another's slave girl.

The Prophet (ﷺ) also interceded for a lover so that his beloved would continue her relationship with him by marrying him, but she refused. This was in the story of Mughith and Barira: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him walking behind her with tears streaming down his cheeks, he said to her: 'If only you would return to him?' She said: 'Are you commanding me, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, I am only interceding.' She said: 'I have no need of him.' He then said to his uncle: 'O Abbas, are you not amazed at Mughith's love for Barira and her hatred for him?' He did not condemn his love for her, even though she had already separated from him."

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to treat his wives equally in the division of his time and would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what I do not possess." He meant love. Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿You will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [al-Nisa: 129], meaning in love and intercourse.

The rightly-guided caliphs and the merciful among the people never ceased to intercede for lovers with their beloved whose union was permissible, as was previously mentioned in the actions of Abu Bakr and Uthman. Likewise, Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was brought a young Arab man who had been found in the house of some people at night. He said to him: "What is your story?" He said: "I am not a thief, but I will tell you the truth:"

*I was attached in the house of al-Riyahi to a graceful maiden,*
*before whose beauty the full moon humbles itself.*
*Among the daughters of the Romans she has beauty and a figure;*
*when she takes pride in her beauty, pride itself is in awe of her.*
*When I came to the house, from the heat of my heart,*
*I spent the night, while within it the embers of her blaze burned.*
*The people of the house rushed at me, then they cried out:*
*"He is the thief, for whom death and capture are decreed."*

When Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) heard his poetry, he was moved by it and said to al-Muhallab ibn Rabah: "Let him have her." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, ask him who he is." He said: "Al-Nahhas ibn Uyayna." He said: "Take her, she is yours."

Mu'awiya bought a slave girl and was greatly enamoured of her. One day he heard her reciting some verses from it:

*I parted from him like a branch swaying in the dust,*
*radiant and handsome, after his moustache had grown.*

He asked her, and she informed him that she loved her master. So he returned her to him, though there remained something of her in his heart.

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned about Rabi'a that Zubayda read on a wall on the road to Makkah:

*Is there not, among the servants of Allah or among His maidservants,*
*a generous one who removes the grief of the one whose reason has departed?*
*He has an eye: as for the eyelids, they are wounded;*
*and as for the inner self, the fire of it is upon one foot.*

So she vowed to devise a way to find its author, if she knew him, so that she could unite him with the one he loved. While she was at Muzdalifa, she heard someone reciting them, so she sought him. He claimed that he had composed them about a paternal cousin of his whose family had vowed not to marry her to him. She sent word to the tribe and kept offering them money until they married her to him. The woman was more passionately in love with him than he was with her. Zubayda counted this among her greatest good deeds and would say: "I am not anything more delighted than my bringing together of that young man and young woman."

Al-Kharaʾiti said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik had a young male slave and a female slave who loved each other. One day the young man wrote to her:

*I saw you in a dream, as if you had given me*
*the cool saliva from your mouth.*
*It was as if your hand was in mine, and as if we*
*had spent the night together on one bed.*
*So I spent my whole day drowsing,*
*wanting to see you in my sleep, yet I was not sleeping.*

The female slave answered him:

*You have seen good, and all that you have seen*
*you will attain from me, despite the envious.*
*Indeed I hope that you will embrace me,*
*and spend the night with me upon a full breast.*
*And I will see you between my anklets and my bracelets,*
*and I will see you above my breasts and my body.*

When this reached Sulayman, he married her to the young man and treated them well, despite his great jealousy.

Jami' ibn Birkhiyya said: "I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, the mufti of Madina: 'Is there any sin in a love that has overtaken us?'" Sa'id said: "One is only blamed for what is within one's power." Then Sa'id said: "By Allah, no one has asked me about this, and if someone had asked me, I would not have answered except with this."

(Section)

Passionate love for women is of three kinds:

The first is one which is a act of devotion and obedience, which is love for one's wife and one's slave girl. This love is beneficial, for it leads more to the purposes for which Allah legislated marriage, and it restrains the gaze and the heart from looking towards other than one's own household. For this reason, such a lover is praised by Allah and by people.

The second is passion which is detested by Allah and is distance from His mercy. It is the most harmful thing to the servant in his religion and his worldly life. This is the love of beardless youths. No one is afflicted by it except one who has fallen from the sight of Allah and been driven from His door, and whose heart has been distanced from Him. It is among the greatest veils that cut one off from Allah. As one of the righteous predecessors (al-Salaf) said: "When a servant falls from the sight of Allah, He afflicts him with love for beardless youths." This love is what brought upon the people of Lut what it brought upon them, and they were only destroyed through this passion. Allah, exalted is He, said:

﴿By your life, they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.﴾ [al-Hijr: 72].

The remedy for this disease is seeking help from the Turner of Hearts, sincere turning to Him, occupying oneself with His remembrance, substituting love for Him and closeness to Him, and reflecting on the pain that this passion brings and the pleasure that is lost through it, so that the loss of the greatest beloved and the attainment of the greatest hated thing follows from it. When the soul proceeds to this and prefers it, then let him say the takbir over his own self as one says it over a funeral, and let him know that affliction has encompassed him.

The third kind is permissible passion, which occurs without intention, such as the passion of one to whom a beautiful woman is described, or who sees her suddenly without intending to, so that his heart becomes attached to her, and this passion does not cause him any sin. This one is not held accountable and is not punished. The most beneficial thing for him is to resist it and to occupy himself with what is more beneficial for him than it. He must observe concealment, chastity, and patience in the trial, so Allah will make him firm in that, and will compensate him for his patience for the sake of Allah and his chastity, and his abandoning the obedience of his desire, and his preferring the pleasure of Allah and what is with Him.

[Section: The Divisions of People in Passion]

People in passion are of three kinds:

Among them is one who loves absolute beauty, whose heart wanders in every valley, and who has a desire in every beautiful form.

Among them is one who loves restricted beauty, whether he hopes for union with her or not.

Among them is one who loves only the one from whom he hopes for union.

There is a difference in strength and weakness among these three types.

The lover of absolute beauty: his heart wanders in every valley, and he has a desire in every beautiful form:

*One day at Hazwara, one day at al-Aqiq, and at al-Udhayb one day, and one day at al-Khulayṣa.*

*And at times he heads for Najd, and at other times for the valley of al-Aqiq, and at other times the palace of Taymaʾ.*

So his passion is more widespread, but it is not stable, and it shifts often:

*He is enamoured with this one, then he loves another, and forgets them by the time morning comes.*

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 30 (Ar-Rum), verse 21 (part 2 of 2):

The lover of beauty that is bound (in a lawful, committed bond) is more steadfast toward his beloved and more enduring in his love for her, and his love is stronger than the love of the first, because the two are gathered in one object. However, what weakens both of them is the absence of hope for union. The lover of beauty whose union is hoped for is the most intelligent and most knowing of lovers, and his love is stronger, because hope sustains it and strengthens it.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 30, verse 28:

He (subhanahu) argues against them with what is in their intellects of the ugliness of one of them having a slave as a partner to himself. For if one of you finds it abhorrent that his slave should be his partner, and does not accept that, then how do you make for Me, from among My slaves, partners whom you worship as you worship Me?

This shows that the ugliness of worshipping other than Allah ta'ala is firmly established in the intellects and the natural disposition (fitra), and that revelation (al-sam') alerted the intellects and guided them to recognise what was deposited in them of the ugliness of that.

(Section)

Know that the worshipper venerates his object of worship, is devoted to it (mutaallih), and is submissive and humbled before it. The Lord, exalted is He, alone is deserving of perfect veneration, majesty, devotion (ta'alluh), submission and humility. This is the exclusive right of His, so among the worst forms of injustice is to give His right to another, or to associate another with Him in it, especially when the one made a partner in His right is His own servant and slave, as Allah ta'ala said: ﴿He has set forth for you an example from yourselves. Do you have among what your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear your own selves? Thus do We detail the verses for a people who use reason.﴾ [al-Rum: 28].

That is: if one of you is too proud to have his slave as a partner in his provision, then how do you make for Me, from among My slaves, partners in that in which I am alone? That is divinity (al-ilahiyyah), which is not fitting for other than Me and not valid for anyone besides Me.

Whoever claims this has not measured Me with my true measure, nor venerated Me with my true veneration, nor singled Me out with what I am singled out with, alone, apart from My creation. Thus whoever worships another alongside Him has not measured Allah with His true measure.

(Section)

The words of Allah ta'ala: ﴿He has set forth for you an example from yourselves. Do you have among what your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear your own selves? Thus do We detail the verses for a people who use reason (28)﴾

This is an analogical argument (dalil qiyas) with which Allah subhanahu argued against the polytheists, since they made for Him partners from among His servants and His possession. He established against them a proof whose soundness they recognise from their own selves, requiring nothing from outside them. Among the most eloquent forms of argument is to take the person from himself and argue against him with what is within himself, established in his own estimation and known to him. So He said: "Do you have among what your right hands possess, of your male and female slaves, any partners in property and family?" That is: do your slaves share with you in your wealth and your households, so that you and they are equal in that, fearing that they will divide your wealth with you and share it out, and take some of it for themselves over you, as a partner fears his partner? Ibn Abbas said: "fearing them" means fearing that they will inherit from you as some of you inherit from others. The meaning is: does any one of you consent that his slave be a partner to him in his wealth and household, to the point of equality with him in disposing of that, so that he fears to be alone in his wealth in a matter over which he would dispose, as he fears other partners and free men? If you do not accept that for yourselves, why then do you equate with Me from among My creation one who is a slave belonging to Me? If this judgment is false in your natural dispositions and intellects, though it is possible and permissible for you, since your slaves are not truly your property but are your brothers whom Allah placed under your hands while you and they are slaves to Me, then how do you permit such a judgment regarding My right, when those you have made partners to Me are My slaves, My possession and My creation? Thus is the detailing of the verses for people of understanding.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 30, verse 30 (part 1 of 3):**

*"Hanifan"* (inclining, upright) is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) that confirms the meaning of God's words ﴿So direct your face toward the religion﴾. For this reason it has been explained as "sincere" (*mukhlisan*), so the verse includes both truthfulness (*sidq*) and sincerity (*ikhlas*).

Directing one's face toward the religion means devoting one's pursuit of it entirely, so that no desire for anything else remains in the heart. The *hanif* is one who is single-minded and wants nothing else. Truthfulness means that your seeking is not divided, and single-mindedness means that what you seek is not divided. The first is the unity of the seeker (*tawhid al-talab*), and the second is the unity of the sought (*tawhid al-matlub*).

**(Section)**

In the two *Sahihs* (al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every child is born upon the *fitrah* (innate disposition). Then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete young. Do you see any mutilation in it? [Mutilation comes] only when you mutilate it." Then Abu Hurayrah recited: ﴿The nature (fitrah) of God, upon which He created mankind. There is no alteration in the creation of God﴾.

In another wording: "There is no child born except upon this *millah* (religion)."

The scholars have differed about the meaning of this *fitrah* and what is intended by it. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said, concerning the meaning of *fitrah*: "There are two narrations from Ahmad (ibn Hanbal):

The first: it is the acknowledgment of knowing God, Exalted is He. This is the covenant that God took from them in the loins of their fathers, when He wiped over the back of Adam and brought forth from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection like particles, and made them bear witness against themselves: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we bear witness.﴾

Thus no one exists who does not acknowledge that he has a Creator and Governor, even if he names Him by other than His name. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, 'God'﴾. So every child is born upon that first acknowledgment."

He said: "*Fitrah* here does not mean Islam, for two reasons:

First: the meaning of *fitrah* is the beginning of creation, and from it comes God's saying: ﴿Originator (Fatir) of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning their initiator. Since *fitrah* is the beginning, it must be that which occurred at the first creation, and which took place in the innate nature of understanding, namely their being brought forth as offspring, because that is the state of their origin. Also, if *fitrah* here meant Islam, then whenever a child is born to two disbelieving parents, he would not inherit from them or they from him while he is a child, because he would be a Muslim, and difference of religion prevents inheritance. And it would not be valid to enslave him, nor would he be judged Muslim by his father's Islam, because he would be a Muslim."

He said: "This is the interpretation of Ibn Qutaybah, and Ibn Battah mentioned it in *al-Ibanah*."

He said: "Not everyone who is granted knowledge is judged to be Muslim, such as adult disbelievers, for knowledge is present in them and yet they are not Muslims."

He said: "Ahmad indicated this interpretation. In the narration of al-Maymuni, he said: 'The first *fitrah* upon which people were created.' Al-Maymuni said to him: 'The *fitrah* is the religion.' He said: 'Yes.'"

Al-Qadi said: "Ahmad meant by religion the knowledge we have mentioned."

He said: The second narration: "*Fitrah* here is the beginning of his creation in his mother's womb, because interpreting it as the covenant that He took from them, which is the acknowledgment of His knowledge, is interpreting *fitrah* as Islam, since acknowledging knowledge of God is acknowledging faith, and the believer is a Muslim. And if *fitrah* were Islam, then whenever a child was born to two disbelieving parents, they would not inherit from him nor he from them."

He said: "And also, that would prevent disbelief from being a creation of God, whereas the principles of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) are contrary to that."

He said: "Ahmad also indicated this in the narration of Ali ibn Sa'id, when he was asked about the saying: 'Every child is born upon the *fitrah*.' He said: 'Upon happiness and misery.' Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kahhal narrated that he asked him, and he said: 'It is the *fitrah* upon which God created people, wretched or happy.' Jubayl also narrated from him: 'The *fitrah* upon which God created the servants is from misery and happiness.' He said: 'All this indicates from his words that the meaning of *fitrah* here is the beginning of his creation in his mother's womb.'"

Our shaykh Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah said: "[Ahmad] did not mention the first covenant, but said: 'The first *fitrah* upon which people were created,' and it is the religion."

He also said in another place: "If a disbeliever's parents, or one of them, die, he is judged to be Muslim, and [Ahmad] cited this hadith as evidence. This shows that he interpreted the hadith as meaning that he is born upon the *fitrah* of Islam, as is clearly stated in the hadith. If *fitrah* were not Islam in his view, his citing of the hadith would not be valid."

And his saying in another place: "Being born upon what one is created with, of misery and happiness, does not contradict this. God, Glorified is He, decreed happiness and misery, wrote them, and decreed that they would occur through causes by which they come about, such as the action of parents. The Judaizing, Christianizing, and Magianizing of parents is something God has decreed that they do to the child. The child is born upon the *fitrah*, sound, but also born with the fact that his parents will alter this sound *fitrah*, as God, Glorified is He, has decreed and written. The Prophet (ﷺ) illustrated this with his saying: 'Just as an animal gives birth to a complete young, do you see any mutilation in it?'

He made clear that the animal is born sound, then a human mutilates it, and that is by God's decree and destiny. Likewise the child is born upon the *fitrah*, sound, then his parents corrupt him, and that too is by God's decree and destiny."

Ahmad and other imams only said "upon what he was created with, of misery or happiness," because the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyya, a early theological school who denied divine predestination of human acts) argue with this hadith that disbelief and sins are not by God's decree and destiny, but are things people originate. For this reason they said to Malik ibn Anas: "The Qadariyyah argue against us with the beginning of the hadith." He said: "Argue against them with its end," which is the saying: "God knows best what they were doing."

Ahmad and others made clear that there is no proof in it for the Qadariyyah, for they do not say that the parents themselves created their Judaizing and Christianizing. Rather, the child becomes Jewish or Christian by his own choice, and the parents were only a cause of this through teaching and instruction. If this consideration is attributed to them, then it is even more fitting to attribute it to God, who is the Creator of everything. For although He created him born upon the sound *fitrah*, He also decreed what would happen to him afterwards, of change, and knew it, as in the authentic hadith:

"The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed on the day he was sealed as a disbeliever. Had he reached adulthood, he would have burdened his parents with rebellion and disbelief."

So his saying "sealed on the day he was sealed" means: decreed and decided in the Book that he would disbelieve, not that his disbelief existed before he was born or at the time of his birth, for he was born upon the sound *fitrah*. And whoever thinks that the sealing on his heart is the sealing mentioned on the hearts of disbelievers is mistaken, for that cannot be said to be "sealed on the day he was sealed," since the sealing on the heart only occurs after disbelief.

It is authentically established in Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Hammad, on the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he related from his Lord, Blessed and Exalted is He, that He said: "I created My servants as *hunafa'* (upright in faith), all of them, then the devils seduced them, forbade them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for."

This is explicit that He created them upon *hanifiyyah* (uprightness), and that the devils seduced them afterwards. Likewise in the hadith of al-Aswad ibn Sari', which Ahmad and others narrated:

He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) sent a military expedition, and the killing led them to kill the children. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: 'What prompted you to kill the children?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, were they not the children of polytheists?' He said: 'Are not your best the children of polytheists?' Then the Prophet (ﷺ) stood to deliver a sermon and said: 'Indeed every child is born upon the *fitrah* until his tongue speaks for him.'"

His sermon to them with this hadith, following his prohibition to them about killing the children of polytheists, and his saying to them, "Are not your best the children of polytheists?", is explicit that he meant those who were born not disbelievers, and then disbelief arose afterwards.

Had he intended that the child, at birth, is either Muslim or disbeliever according to what destiny had already determined for him, then what was mentioned would not be proof for the prohibition he intended against killing the children of polytheists.

Some have thought that the meaning of his saying "Are not your best the children of polytheists?" is that it may be known to God that if they had lived, they would have believed, so the prohibition refers to this meaning of possibility.

This is not the meaning of the hadith. Rather its meaning is that your best are the foremost (*al-sabiqun al-awwalun*), and these were among the children of polytheists, for their fathers were disbelievers, then the sons later became Muslims. A child is not harmed by being among the children of polytheists if he is a believer, for God rewards him only for his own deeds and not for the deeds of his parents, and He brings the believer out of the disbeliever, and the disbeliever out of the believer, as He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living.

**(Question)**

If it is said: the boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed on the day he was sealed as a disbeliever. And Noah said about his people: ﴿They will not beget any but wicked disbelievers﴾.

And in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The children of Adam were created in various classes. Among them is one who is born a believer, lives a believer, and dies a believer, and among them is one who is born a disbeliever, lives a disbeliever, and dies a disbeliever..." (the hadith)?

It is answered: This does not contradict his being born upon the *fitrah*. For he was sealed and born with his disbelief decreed, if he were to reason; otherwise, at the time of his birth he does not know disbelief or faith. So this is a decreed state, not a state accompanying the agent. Thus he is born upon the *fitrah*, and born a disbeliever in two valid, established respects: the first is in receptivity and preference for Islam if left alone, and the second is in action and will when he reasons. If you combine the preceding *fitrah*, the lofty preceding mercy, the far-reaching wisdom, and the complete self-sufficiency, and connect his *fitrah*, mercy, wisdom, and self-sufficiency, the matter will become clear to you.

**(Section)**

God, Glorified is He, has bestowed upon His servants, as part of His beneficence and blessings, two matters which are the foundation of happiness:

The first: that He created them, at the origin of their creation, upon the sound *fitrah*. So every child is born upon the *fitrah* until his parents are the ones who take him out of it, as has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ), who likened this to an animal coming forth sound and whole until its owner mutilates it. It is also established from him that he said: "God says: 'I created My servants as *hunafa'*, then the devils came to them and diverted them from their religion, forbade them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for.'"

So when the soul is left to its *fitrah*, it does not prefer anything over love of its Creator and Originator, nor over worshipping Him alone. It does not associate anything with Him, nor deny the perfection of His lordship. It finds Him the most beloved of things, the most obedient to it, and the most preferred. But those devils of jinn and mankind who accompany it, through their adornment and misguidance, corrupt it until its inclination and judgment are overwhelmed.

The second matter: God, Glorified is He, guided people with a general guidance, by placing in them the knowledge (*ma'rifah*) and enabling them with its causes, by sending down Books to them, sending Messengers to them, and teaching them what they did not know. In every soul is that which requires knowing the truth and loving it. God has guided every servant to kinds of knowledge by which he can reach the happiness of the Hereafter, and placed in his nature a love for that. But a servant may turn away from seeking knowledge of what benefits him, so he does not desire it nor know it. His not desiring it and not knowing it is a privative matter (*amr 'adami*), so it is not attributed to the Lord, neither this nor that, for from this aspect it is an evil. What is attributed to the Lord is His knowledge of it, and His decree concerning it by not willing its opposite, and His leaving it in its original privation. From this aspect it is good, for knowledge of evil is better than ignorance of it, and not removing it by establishing its opposite is good if it is required by wisdom, even though it is evil with respect to its locus. The complete explanation of this will come in the chapter on the entry of evil into the divine decree, God willing, Glorified is He.

**[Section on the meaning of *fitrah*]**

If it is said: All of this is built by you on the premise that the first *fitrah* is the *fitrah* of Islam. But Ahmad has explicitly stated that *fitrah* is what people were created upon of misery and happiness. He said in the narration of al-Hasan ibn Thawab: "Every child of polytheists is born upon the *fitrah*, upon the *fitrah* upon which God created him, of misery and happiness that preceded in the Book. Return on this matter to the origin." This is its meaning.

And he said in the narration of Hanbal, Abu al-Harith, and al-Fadl ibn Ziyad: "The *fitrah* upon which the servants were created is of misery and happiness."

And he said in the narration of Ali ibn Sa'id, when he was asked about the hadith "Every child is born upon the *fitrah*": "Upon happiness and misery, and to it he returns according to what he was created."

Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kahhal said: "I said to Abu Abd Allah (Ahmad): 'What is the explanation of "Every child is born upon the *fitrah*"?' He said: 'It is the *fitrah* upon which God created people, wretched or happy.'" And if this is his explicit statement on *fitrah*, how would he conceal, with respect to his school (*madhhab*) regarding children, that they are upon Islam by the death of their parents?
